notes.summary: Static GK gives 2–3 questions: sports (players per team, trophies, terms), national awards, books and authors, and important days. These are pure memory facts — revise them with flashcards.

concepts.title: National awards
concepts.body:
• Bharat Ratna: highest civilian award, instituted in 1954. First recipients: C. Rajagopalachari, Dr. S. Radhakrishnan and Dr. C.V. Raman.
  • Dadasaheb Phalke Award: cinema; first given in 1969 to Devika Rani.
  • Jnanpith Award: literature; first given in 1965 to G. Sankara Kurup (Malayalam).
  • Sports: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna (highest sports honour; renamed in 2021), Arjuna Award (sportspersons), Dronacharya Award (coaches).

varieties.name: Sports facts
varieties.how: Recall team size, the sport for each trophy, and sport-specific terms.

example.q: The Thomas Cup is associated with which sport?
steps: Thomas Cup = men's badminton team championship

varieties.name: Awards and books
varieties.how: Pair each award with its field and first winner; pair each book with its author.

steps: Written by Jawaharlal Nehru in Ahmednagar Fort jail (1944)

varieties.name: Important days
varieties.how: Link the day to the person or event behind it — that makes the date easy to recall.

example.q: National Science Day is celebrated on:
steps: It marks C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect

tips: Birthday days: 12 Jan Vivekananda, 29 Aug Dhyan Chand, 5 Sep Radhakrishnan, 14 Nov Nehru.
Badminton trophies: Thomas = men, Uber = women.
Durand Cup is the oldest football tournament in Asia.
traps: National Science Day (28 Feb) is not C.V. Raman's birthday; it marks his discovery.
Ranji Trophy is cricket, Santosh Trophy is football — both are domestic Indian tournaments.
Dronacharya Award is for coaches, Arjuna Award for players.

questions.q: How many players are there on each side in a volleyball match?
questions.solution:
Volleyball has 6 players per side on court. Basketball has 5 and kabaddi has 7.
Memory hook: Volleyball court has 2 rows of 3 = 6.

questions.q: National Sports Day in India is celebrated on the birthday of:
questions.solution:
National Sports Day is on 29 August, the birthday of hockey wizard Major Dhyan Chand.
Memory hook: The Khel Ratna also carries his name — Dhyan Chand owns Indian sports honours.

Rabindranath Tagore wrote Gitanjali; its English version won him the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
Memory hook: Gitanjali = 'song offerings' by Gurudev Tagore.

questions.q: The Durand Cup is associated with which sport?
questions.solution:
The Durand Cup is a football tournament, one of the oldest in the world and the oldest in Asia (first held in 1888).
Memory hook: Durand and Santosh — India's two classic football cups.

questions.q: Who was the first recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award?
questions.solution:
Devika Rani received the first Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 1969. She is called the 'First Lady of Indian Cinema'.
Memory hook: First award, First Lady of Indian Cinema.

questions.q: National Science Day is celebrated on 28 February to mark:
questions.solution:
C.V. Raman announced the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928. His birthday is 7 November.
Memory hook: Science Day celebrates the discovery, not the man's birthday.

questions.q: Which of the following was NOT among the first recipients of the Bharat Ratna in 1954?
questions.solution:
The first Bharat Ratna awards (1954) went to C. Rajagopalachari, Dr. S. Radhakrishnan and Dr. C.V. Raman. Nehru received it in 1955.
Memory hook: 'R-R-R': Rajagopalachari, Radhakrishnan, Raman.

options: Wings of Fire — A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
questions.solution:
'India Wins Freedom' is the autobiography of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad. Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India'.
Memory hook: Azad = freedom; 'India Wins Freedom' belongs to Azad.
